s: A company's solutions architect needs to provide secure Remote Desktop connectivity to users for Amazon EC2 Windows instances that are hosted in a VPC. The solution must integrate centralized user management with the company's on-premises Active Directory. Connectivity to the VPC is through the internet. The company has hardware that can be used to establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
o: Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory.Deploy an EC2 instance as a bastion host in the VPC. Ensure that the EC2 instance is joined to the domain. Use the bastion host to access the target instances through RDP.

Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to integrate with the on-premises Active Directory by using the AWS Directory Service for MicrosoftActive Directory AD Connector. Configure permission sets against user groups for access to AWS Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Fleet Manager to access the target instances through RDP.

Implement a VPN between the on-premises environment and the target VPC. Ensure that the target instances are joined to the on-premises Active Directory domain over the VPN connection. Configure RDP access through the VPN. Connect from the company's network to the target instances.

Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory.Deploy a Remote Desktop Gateway on AWS by using an AWS Quick Start. Ensure that the Remote Desktop Gateway is joined to the domain. Use the Remote Desktop Gateway to access the target instances through RDP.

w.y: The key uses the traditional pattern: AWS Managed Microsoft AD trusts the on-premises AD, and a domain-joined Remote Desktop Gateway gives secure RDP over the internet with centralized AD users. Be aware this is debated. Option B (Fleet Manager RDP with IAM Identity Center and AD Connector) avoids running Managed AD and gateway servers and may be cheaper. D is the answer most dumps accept.

o.A: A bastion host is less secure than an RD Gateway (it exposes RDP directly) and still needs Managed AD.
o.B: Plausible and possibly cheaper (Fleet Manager is free, AD Connector costs less than Managed AD), but AD Connector still needs a VPN and the option doesn't mention one.
o.C: Users would have to be on the company network, so it doesn't give internet-based remote access for users elsewhere.
o.D: Key answer: Managed AD with a trust plus a domain-joined RD Gateway gives secure, centrally managed RDP over the internet.

s: Connecting to a Windows Server managed instance using Remote Desktop - AWS Systems Manager

nt: Debated. Fleet Manager RDP through Identity Center with AD Connector (B) avoids running Managed AD and Remote Desktop Gateway servers and may be cheaper. The key's D is the traditional pattern.
